# MIGRATION SPEC — OpenAI Python SDK v0.x → v1.x

(As given verbatim to each Target A detection agent on 2026-08-18. The

facts.text: Module-level client configuration is removed in v1. Bare module-level attribute assignments `openai.api_key = ...`, `openai.api_base = ...`, and `openai.organization = ...` no longer configure the client; they must be replaced by constructing an explicit client object, e.g. `client = OpenAI(api_key=...)`.

All module-level namespaced call patterns of the form `openai.<Namespace>.create(...)`, plus the equivalent `.list(...)` and `.retrieve(...)` calls, are removed in v1. Named examples given: `openai.ChatCompletion.create(...)`, `openai.Completion.create(...)`, `openai.Embedding.create(...)`, `openai.Image.create(...)`, `openai.Moderation.create(...)`. These must migrate to client-based calls, e.g. `client.chat.completions.create(...)`.

The `openai.error` submodule is removed in v1. Exception classes that lived there — e.g. `openai.error.RateLimitError`, `openai.error.ServiceUnavailableError`, `openai.error.InvalidRequestError`, `openai.error.AuthenticationError`, and others — now live at the top level of the `openai` package (e.g. `openai.RateLimitError`). Any reference to `openai.error.*` must change.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE / NOT a breaking change: response-object access patterns. Whether code reads a response via dict-style access (`response['choices']`) or attribute-style access (`response.choices`), both remain valid and must not be flagged; this migration does not touch that.

The three changes listed (module-level config attributes, module-level namespaced calls, and `openai.error` submodule) are the ONLY confirmed breaking changes in this migration; anything not described is unaffected.
Affected sites include those reached indirectly through a repository's own helper functions — call chains must be traced, not just the entry-point file grepped.
